newsitem.title: CANADA: Good Prairie crop output seen in 90-day forecast.
newsitem.headline: Good Prairie crop output seen in 90-day forecast.

text.p: Production prospects for crops on Canada's Prairies were favorable based on Environment Canada's 90-day forecast released Sunday, meteorologists said.

"Near normal temperatures is our forecast for the Prairie grainbelt with above normal precipitation forecast for the eastern two-thirds of Alberta and western half to two-thirds of Saskatchewan," Environment Canada's Winnipeg Climate Centre superintendent Brian Fehr told Reuters.
Normal rainfall was expected on the rest of the grainbelt.
Prairie temperature and rain normals are based on measurements taken from 1961 to 1990, Fehr said.
"Great. You can't beat it for a forecast," Canadian Wheat Board weather and crop surveillance director Paul Bullock said. "If you want lots of grain, that's the way to make it."
All wheat seeded area on the Prairies was seen 9.2 percent down at 28.22 million acres in 1997 from 31.08 millioin acres the year before, Statistics Canada said April 30.
Canola seeded area was seen up 32 percent to 11.585 million acres from 8.8 million, StatsCan said.
The federal agency's next seeding intentions report is due June 27 at 0730 CDT/1230 GMT but United Grain Growers plans to issue its plantings report on June 11 at 1400 CDT/1900 GMT.
The area forecast to see more rain than normal is the arid Palliser Triangle where 75 percent of Canada's durum is grown.

The area bounded by Swift Current, Sask., to the southeast, Rosetown, Sask., to the north and Medicine Hat, Alta., to the southwest saw average rainfall of 128 to 153 mm (6 inches) between June 1 and August 31 from 1961 to 1990.
Average highs recorded in that period were 17.2 Celsius (63 F) on the Saskatchewan side, 18.7 Celsius (66 F) on the Alberta side, Environment Canada said.

"Durum does better in dry conditions but if you give it moderate temperatures and lots of water so if you're looking at that for the Palliser Triangle you're looking at above average durum yields," Bullock said.
